question: H₂SO₄ is the chemical formula for __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Oil of Vitriol.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oil of Vitriol **is an **old term** for sulfuric acid, and **H₂SO₄** is indeed the chemical formula for **sulfuric acid.**
 
• It is a **highly corrosive and strong acid **commonly used in various industrial processes, such as **battery production, fertilizers, and chemical synthesis.**
 
• Oil of Vitriol was historically used in **alchemy and early chemical experiments**.
 
• The term "oil" in its name refers to the **oily texture **of concentrated sulfuric acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Vitriol:**

 
 
• Green Vitriol refers to **iron(II) sulfate**, which has the chemical formula** FeSO₄.**
 
• It is a **green-coloured salt **that can be found in nature as mineral, but it can also be prepared by **dissolving iron in sulfuric acid**.
 
• Green Vitriol is used in various applications, including **water treatment, dyes, pigments, and as a fertilizer.**
 
 
 
• **Muriatic Acid:**
 
 
• Muriatic Acid is an alternative name for **hydrochloric acid**, which has the chemical formula** HCl.**
 
• HCl is a strong, corrosive acid that is widely used in chemical laboratories,** metal cleaning, and pickling processes.**
 
• The term **"muriatic"** comes from** "muria,"** which means **brine or saltwater**, as hydrochloric acid was historically produced from salt.
 
 
 
• **Blue Vitriol:**
 
 
• **Blue Vitriol** refers to **copper(II) sulfate**, with the chemical formula **CuSO₄.**
 
• It is a blue-coloured crystalline salt that is used in various applications, such as agriculture as a **fungicide and herbicide, in electroplating, and as a laboratory reagent.**
 
• Blue Vitriol has been historically used for various purposes, including **dyeing, tanning, and in medicine as an astringent.**
